key_facts: These notes apply to all teams and officials at the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix on 13-15 March 2026.
The notes set out procedural requirements for safe and orderly conduct of the competition, including rules about pit lane access, starting procedures, driver weighing, and track limits.

Key safety requirements include: drivers must allow faster cars past when lapped; drivers must not proceed erratically when a safety car is returning to the pits; pit lane team personnel must only be present when needed for work; and drivers exceeding a maximum time between safety car lines may be penalised for going unnecessarily slowly.
Practice starts are not allowed at pit exit but are permitted on the grid during free practice and on the pit exit road during reconnaissance laps.
The circuit has been modified: the kerb at Turn 3 apex has been reduced in height, the tyre barrier at Turn 7 on the left has been realigned, and TSP 17 has been moved to 100m before Turn 14.
plain_explanation:
These are procedural instructions for the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix at Shanghai International Circuit, issued on 12 March 2026. The notes cover the rules teams and drivers must follow to ensure the competition runs safely and in order.

Drivers who are caught by a faster car must allow that car past at the first available opportunity. The marshalling system will give a warning when a faster car is within 3.0 seconds, and blue light panels will be shown when the faster car is within 1.2 seconds. When a safety car (a vehicle brought onto the track to slow drivers down and bunch them up during hazardous conditions) is returning to the pits after an orange lights (an instruction from the safety car to drivers to prepare for restart) are turned off, drivers must proceed without erratic acceleration, braking, or other manoeuvres that could endanger others.

During qualifying sessions and practice, drivers may not exceed a maximum time from the Second Safety Car Line to the First Safety Car Line on any lap. This applies to out-laps and in-laps (laps leaving and returning to the garage). If a driver exceeds this time, they may be penalised for going unnecessarily slowly. The maximum time will be told to teams and drivers after the practice session.

In the pit lane, team personnel are only allowed immediately before they are needed to work on a car and must leave as soon as work is complete. For the race only, this rule applies until all cars that can do so have finished and entered the parc fermé (a sealed area where cars are held under observation). After the race ends and the Race Director says it is safe, a message will tell pass holders they may access the pit lane.

Practice starts (standing starts practised before the race) may not be done at pit exit. They are allowed on the grid after free practice and on the pit exit road during reconnaissance laps (exploratory laps before the race), but not during qualifying. When practice starts happen on the pit exit road, cars wanting to do a practice start must stay left and stop at the white line; cars not doing one must cross to the track at the earliest chance.

Before each session starts, cars may not enter the pit lane to go to pit exit until 5 minutes before the session begins. If a session is stopped and restarted, cars may only enter the fast lane (the lane closer to the racing surface) after the restart time is confirmed by official messaging.

Drivers finishing in the top 10 must be weighed immediately after they leave their cars and before touching anyone. Other drivers who finish must go to the scales straight away after returning to their garage. Drivers may not drink or do anything that increases their weight before being weighed.

The circuit has three changes for this event. The back of the kerb (the edge of the track) at the apex of Turn 3 has been made lower. The tyre barrier at Turn 7 on the left side has been moved to a new position. Safety pole TSP 17, which sits before Turn 14, has been moved 100 metres further back.
